subject: Proposed Condominium Conversion Ordinance
overview: The subcommittee deliberated on a draft ordinance to regulate the conversion of rental units into condominiums, focusing on tenant protections and displacement mitigation. The body reviewed local conversion data and discussed specific provisions regarding notice periods, relocation payments, and administrative oversight.

items.title: Introduction to Condominium Conversion Ordinance
items.summary: The subcommittee convened to discuss paper 22-321, a proposed legislative mechanism to regulate the conditions under which rental units are converted into condominiums.

items.title: Presentation of Medford Conversion Data
items.summary: A representative from Planning, Development and Sustainability (PDS) presented research showing an average of approximately 30 condominium conversions per year in Medford since 2018, primarily involving multi-family dwellings.

items.title: Building Department Technical Feedback
items.summary: Interim Building Commissioner Bill Forte provided preliminary comments on permit tracking systems and confirmed that affordable units with state restrictive covenants generally cannot be converted.

items.title: Deliberation on Notice Periods and Purchase Rights
items.summary: Members discussed extending notice requirements for protected tenants to five years and established a preference for including a tenant right of first refusal to purchase converted units.

items.title: Relocation Payments and Assistance
items.summary: The subcommittee explored tying relocation payments to a formula based on median rent rather than a flat fee to better align with actual moving costs for displaced tenants.

items.title: Conversion Caps and Owner Exemptions
items.summary: Discussion focused on potential annual caps for conversions and creating exemptions for owner-occupants to ensure the ordinance primarily targets for-profit developers.

items.title: Administrative Authority and Legislative Referrals
items.summary: The subcommittee approved motions to request that the Community Development Board serve as the implementing authority and referred legal questions regarding city purchase rights to KP Law.
